items.title: A New Vision for Human Work After Automation
items.text: Hey, welcome back to the Every Podcast, where we talk about the future of work. I'm Natalia Quintero, and at Every, our team of writers and builders use AI every day, so we can tell you how the frontier is shifting, what actually works, and what you need to know. So last week at Every, we hosted our first ever conference, V.C.S.S., It was a full day of talks in Brooklyn featuring speakers from Anthropic, OpenAI, Notion, Lovable, Ode, and many more. If you missed it, we'll have all of the talks available at every.to forward slash TV. We built the whole day around one question. What does great human work look like after automation? Dan Shipper, Every's co-founder and CEO, closed the conference with his answer, which you'll hear later in this episode. items.title: There are basically two kinds of companies to build right now
items.text: There are basically two kinds of companies to build right now. 1. Diffusion of AI This is the "vertical SaaS" of today. There are a bunch of different models for it (FDE company, rollup, horizontal product) but ultimately it all boils down to the same thing: get AI diffused very close to where the work is being done. Profound, Cognition, Harvey etc. A lot of great companies will get built here. 2. Frontier of AI This is where the really interesting action is. Use AI to accelerate scientific progress, then build products from that progress. It is a harder category to see. But we are seeing a lot more of it at @spc: - Externa is adding hundreds of new chemical building blocks to proteins, so...

items.title: I look at what I do with Fable 5
items.text: I look at what I do with Fable 5.2 in the cracks of my week and think: this would've taken five people and $200,000. Then I look at what my team does with the same AI. Last week, between meetings, I analyzed our customer survey, made a game for our team, spotted an opportunity to sell @Every to teams, built a CRM, and started reaching out. Look at that and you might ask: Why would I need a team at all? The chart seems to agree. On OpenAI's GDPval benchmark, AI went from beating human experts 12.4% of the time in 2024 to around 83% in 2026.
